elements.element: If renewal is not automatic, renewal may occur only by mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause expressly provides for automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal period is 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause automatically renews for each additional one-year period, equivalent to 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out by giving no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires sixty days' written notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide Customer a renewal reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires Vendor to provide a renewal reminder.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause renews the existing Agreement without authorizing any renewal price increase, which is more protective than the stated cap.
The clause states that the Agreement shall be automatically renewed on each anniversary.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Either party may prevent continued renewal by providing sixty days' written notice.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase is no more than 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause renews the existing Agreement without authorizing any renewal price increase, which is more protective than a 5% cap.

result.reason: The redline makes only the change needed to reach the fallback by reducing the notice period from 90 to 60 days. It does not meet the preferred automatic-renewal path because Customer does not receive a 30-day opt-out right and Vendor has no reminder duty. Although the fallback is substantively met, drafting quality is reduced because the clause frames the mechanism as termination on 60 days' notice rather than clearly stating a deadline for notice of non-renewal before the anniversary; it also permits a termination date that is not tied to the renewal date.
